personality.summary: Sadistic, theatrical and self-pitying; he casts himself as a victim of normal morality while refusing the one person who truly loved him.
values: being allowed to laugh at others' pain

abilities_owned: self-puppeteered corpse regeneration by threads and debris

relationships.stella-vermillion: Primary target whose grief and righteousness he wants to ruin; she burns him away and refutes his claim that nobody helped him.
relationships.ikki-kurogane: Enemy he fears and hates; kills Ikki to break Stella, but Ikki's delayed cuts cause his final defeat.
relationships.alice-ascaride: Older sister who betrays the world to save him; he mocks her love and only too late is forced to face that he rejected it.
relationships.john-kristoff-von-cobrand: Former puppet prince who first crushes his head after Stella throws him upward.
relationships.lunaeyes-vermillion: One of the people he tries to kill after reviving; she supports John through the execution.
relationships.wallenstein: Rebellion swordsman who discovered his childhood crimes and pushed him to slaughter his village.

periods.summary: Or-Gaule begins the volume fleeing Alice and Stella, then tries to delay Stella with Deus Ex Machina and city-spanning threads. He explains that he has always known he is abnormal and tries to provoke Stella by claiming Alice's protection was merely amusing. Once cornered by Stella's fire wall, he reveals he kept Quedland civilians hidden in underground shelters and uses Marionette to force them into the battlefield. The prepared Vermillion and League troops thwart the hostage tactic, so Stella dismembers him and throws him to John, who destroys his head. Death triggers Or-Gaule's true trump card, Danse Macabre: his corpse reassembles itself with flesh, debris, and threads, concentrates the power once spread across countless puppets, and becomes stronger than before. He strangles Stella, wounds anyone who approaches with Desperado-level inevitability, then tells the story of his childhood as Orles Gaul: a boy unable to feel happiness from kindness, secretly hurting people with puppet powers, found by Wallenstein, and ultimately choosing to massacre his village during his own birthday celebration. Or-Gaule frames morality as violence against him. Ikki interrupts, fights him for one minute, and is killed; Or-Gaule crushes Ikki's head to break Stella. Stella instead controls Ultra Awakening, while Shizuku begins reviving Ikki. In the final exchange Or-Gaule prepares La Grand Guignol, but delayed Kuruizakura cuts planted by Ikki tear open his body and disrupt the attack. Stella pins him with Laevateinn, burns him to ash with Calusaritio Salamander, and condemns him not for being unloved by the world but for rejecting Alice's love.

key_events.summary: Uses civilians as puppets but is dismembered by Stella and head-smashed by John.
Revives as Danse Macabre, reveals his origin, strangles Stella, and kills Ikki.
Fails to complete La Grand Guignol after Ikki's delayed cuts and is burned to ash.
